source.text: אֵ֚לֶּה הָֽעֵדֹ֔ת וְהַֽחֻקִּ֖ים וְהַמִּשְׁפָּטִ֑ים אֲשֶׁ֨ר דִּבֶּ֤ר מֹשֶׁה֙ אֶל־בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: These [are] the testimonies and the statutes and the judgments that spoke Moses to [the] sons of Israel when they came out from Egypt,

en.L: These [are] the testimonies and the statutes and the judgments that Moses spoke to the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel when they came out of Egypt,
en.B: These are the decrees, statutes, and rulings that Moses spoke to the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} after they came out of Egypt,
en.R: These are the solemn instructions, laws, and rules that Moses gave the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} after they came out of Egypt.

es.L: Estos [son] los testimonios y los estatutos y los juicios que Moisés habló a los hijos de Israel cuando salieron de Egipto,
es.B: Estos son los decretos, estatutos y normas que Moisés comunicó a los israelitas después de que salieron de Egipto,
es.R: Estas son las instrucciones solemnes, las leyes y las normas que Moisés dio a los israelitas después de que salieron de Egipto.

fr.L: Ce [sont] les témoignages et les prescriptions et les jugements que Moïse dit aux {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël quand ils sortirent d’Égypte,
fr.B: Voici les décrets, les prescriptions et les règles que Moïse énonça aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} après leur sortie d’Égypte,
fr.R: Voici les instructions solennelles, les lois et les règles que Moïse a données aux {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} après leur sortie d’Égypte.

sw.L: Hizi [ndizo] shuhuda na kanuni na hukumu ambazo Musa aliwaambia wana wa Israeli walipotoka Misri,
sw.B: Haya ndiyo masharti, kanuni na maagizo ambayo Musa aliwaambia Waisraeli baada ya kutoka Misri,
sw.R: Haya ndiyo maelekezo mazito, sheria na maagizo ambayo Musa aliwapa Waisraeli baada ya kutoka Misri.

decisions.choice: testimonies: the solemn terms of the covenant
decisions.reason: The word comes from a root meaning to witness or to declare solemnly. It names the covenant's terms as God's charge to his people (6:17, 20).

decisions.choice: when they came out: in the time after the exodus, on the journey
decisions.reason: Moses spoke these words in the fortieth year after leaving Egypt (1:3). "When they came out" covers the whole period of the journey.

decisions.choice: decrees / solemn instructions
decisions.reason: Balanced says "decrees" and Readable "solemn instructions", since "testimonies" now suggests evidence given in court. Literal keeps "testimonies".

decisions.choice: "shuhuda" (L); "masharti" (B); "maelekezo mazito" (R)
decisions.reason: For the testimonies ('edot): Literal keeps the word of witness, "shuhuda". Balanced says "masharti", the terms of the covenant, because "maagizo" already renders the rulings (mishpatim) in the same list. Readable follows the English "solemn instructions".

source.text: בְּעֵ֨בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֜ן בַּגַּ֗יְא מ֚וּל בֵּ֣ית פְּע֔וֹר בְּאֶ֗רֶץ סִיחֹן֙ מֶ֣לֶךְ הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹשֵׁ֖ב בְּחֶשְׁבּ֑וֹן אֲשֶׁ֨ר הִכָּ֤ה מֹשֶׁה֙ וּבְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בְּצֵאתָ֖ם מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: across the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in [the] land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, whom struck Moses and [the] sons of Israel when they came out from Egypt.

en.L: across the Jordan, in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who dwelt in Heshbon, whom Moses and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel struck down when they came out of Egypt.
en.B: across the Jordan in the valley opposite Beth-peor, in the land of Sihon king of the Amorites, who reigned in Heshbon. Moses and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated him after they came out of Egypt.
en.R: Moses spoke to them on the east side of the Jordan River, in the valley across from Beth-peor. This was in the land of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled from Heshbon. Moses and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} defeated him after they left Egypt.

es.L: al otro lado del Jordán, en el valle frente a Bet-peor, en la tierra de Sijón, rey de los amorreos, que habitaba en Hesbón, al cual derrotaron Moisés y los hijos de Israel cuando salieron de Egipto.
es.B: al otro lado del Jordán, en el valle frente a Bet-peor, en la tierra de Sijón, rey de los amorreos, que reinaba en Hesbón. Moisés y los israelitas lo derrotaron después de salir de Egipto.
es.R: Moisés les habló al lado este del río Jordán, en el valle que está frente a Bet-peor. Era la tierra de Sijón, rey de los amorreos, que gobernaba desde Hesbón. Moisés y los israelitas lo vencieron después de salir de Egipto.

fr.L: au-delà du Jourdain, dans la vallée en face de Beth-Péor, dans le pays de Sihon, roi des Amoréens, qui habitait à Heshbon, que Moïse et les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël frappèrent quand ils sortirent d’Égypte.
fr.B: au-delà du Jourdain, dans la vallée en face de Beth-Péor, dans le pays de Sihon, roi des Amoréens, qui régnait à Heshbon. Moïse et les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} le battirent après leur sortie d’Égypte.
fr.R: Moïse leur a parlé à l’est du Jourdain, dans la vallée en face de Beth-Péor. C’était dans le pays de Sihon, roi des Amoréens, qui régnait depuis Heshbon. Moïse et les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} l’avaient vaincu après leur sortie d’Égypte.

sw.L: ng'ambo ya Yordani, katika bonde lililoelekeana na Beth-peori, katika nchi ya Sihoni mfalme wa Waamori, aliyekaa Heshboni, ambaye Musa na wana wa Israeli walimpiga walipotoka Misri.
sw.B: ng'ambo ya Yordani katika bonde lililoelekeana na Beth-peori, katika nchi ya Sihoni mfalme wa Waamori, aliyetawala Heshboni. Musa na Waisraeli walimshinda baada ya kutoka Misri.
sw.R: Musa aliwaambia maneno haya upande wa mashariki wa Mto Yordani, katika bonde lililo mkabala na Beth-peori. Hii ilikuwa katika nchi ya Sihoni, mfalme wa Waamori, aliyetawala kutoka Heshboni. Musa na Waisraeli walikuwa wamemshinda baada ya kutoka Misri.

decisions.choice: Sihon, whom Moses struck down: the victory of 2:24-37
decisions.reason: Sihon king of Heshbon refused Israel passage and was defeated (2:24-37; Numbers 21:21-31).

decisions.choice: dwelt: lived as king, reigned
decisions.reason: The verb means to sit or dwell. Of a king it means to sit on the throne, to reign (1:4).

decisions.choice: the valley opposite Beth-peor: Israel's camp in Moab
decisions.reason: Beth-peor ("house of Peor") was near the Peor of verse 3. Israel camped in the valley across from it (3:29), and Moses was buried there (34:6).

decisions.choice: Moses spoke to them on the east side of the Jordan River
decisions.reason: Readable, which ended verse 45 with a full stop, repeats that Moses spoke and says plainly that the place was east of the Jordan.

source.text: וַיִּֽירְשׁ֨וּ אֶת־אַרְצ֜וֹ וְאֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ׀ע֣וֹג מֶֽלֶךְ־הַבָּשָׁ֗ן שְׁנֵי֙ מַלְכֵ֣י הָֽאֱמֹרִ֔י אֲשֶׁ֖ר בְּעֵ֣בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּ֑ן מִזְרַ֖ח שָֽׁמֶשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they took possession of his land and [the] land of Og king of Bashan, two kings of the Amorites who [were] across the Jordan toward [the] rising of [the] sun,

en.L: And they took possession of his land and the land of Og king of Bashan, the two kings of the Amorites who [were] across the Jordan toward the rising of the sun,
en.B: They took possession of his land and of the land of Og king of Bashan, those two kings of the Amorites who ruled across the Jordan, toward the sunrise,
en.R: They took possession of Sihon's land and also the land of Og, king of Bashan. These were the two Amorite kings who ruled on the east side of the Jordan River.

es.L: Y tomaron posesión de su tierra y de la tierra de Og, rey de Basán, los dos reyes de los amorreos que [estaban] al otro lado del Jordán, hacia la salida del sol,
es.B: Tomaron posesión de su tierra y de la tierra de Og, rey de Basán, los dos reyes amorreos que reinaban al otro lado del Jordán, hacia el oriente,
es.R: Tomaron posesión de la tierra de Sijón y también de la tierra de Og, rey de Basán. Estos eran los dos reyes amorreos que gobernaban al lado este del río Jordán.

fr.L: Et ils prirent possession de son pays et du pays d’Og, roi du Bashân, les deux rois des Amoréens qui [étaient] au-delà du Jourdain, vers le lever du soleil,
fr.B: Ils prirent possession de son pays et du pays d’Og, roi du Bashân, ces deux rois des Amoréens qui régnaient au-delà du Jourdain, du côté du soleil levant,
fr.R: Ils ont pris possession du pays de Sihon et aussi du pays d’Og, roi du Bashân. C’étaient les deux rois amoréens qui régnaient à l’est du Jourdain.

sw.L: Nao wakaimiliki nchi yake na nchi ya Ogu mfalme wa Bashani, wafalme wawili wa Waamori waliokuwa ng'ambo ya Yordani upande wa mawio ya jua,
sw.B: Waliimiliki nchi yake na nchi ya Ogu mfalme wa Bashani, wale wafalme wawili wa Waamori waliotawala ng'ambo ya Yordani, upande wa mawio ya jua,
sw.R: Waliimiliki nchi ya Sihoni na pia nchi ya Ogu, mfalme wa Bashani. Hawa ndio wale wafalme wawili wa Waamori waliotawala upande wa mashariki wa Mto Yordani.

decisions.choice: Og king of Bashan: the second victory, 3:1-11
decisions.reason: Og came out against Israel at Edrei and was defeated (3:1-11; Numbers 21:33-35). Sihon and Og are often named together (31:4; Psalm 135:11).

decisions.choice: his land: Sihon's land
decisions.reason: "His" points back to Sihon in verse 46.

decisions.choice: Sihon's land
decisions.reason: Readable names Sihon, since its verse 46 ended with another name.

source.text: מֵעֲרֹעֵ֞ר אֲשֶׁ֨ר עַל־שְׂפַת־נַ֧חַל אַרְנֹ֛ן וְעַד־הַ֥ר שִׂיאֹ֖ן ה֥וּא חֶרְמֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: from Aroer which [is] on [the] edge of [the] wadi Arnon and to Mount Siyon, that [is] Hermon,

en.L: from Aroer, which [is] on the edge of the wadi Arnon, and as far as Mount Siyon, that [is] Hermon,
en.B: from Aroer on the edge of the Arnon Valley as far as Mount Siyon, that is, Hermon,
en.R: Their land went from the town of Aroer, at the edge of the Arnon River valley, all the way north to Mount Siyon, which is Mount Hermon.

es.L: desde Aroer, que [está] a la orilla del torrente Arnón, hasta el monte Siyón, que [es] el Hermón,
es.B: desde Aroer, a la orilla del valle del Arnón, hasta el monte Siyón, es decir, el Hermón,
es.R: Su tierra iba desde el pueblo de Aroer, a la orilla del valle del río Arnón, y llegaba por el norte hasta el monte Siyón, que es el monte Hermón.

fr.L: depuis Aroër, qui [est] au bord du torrent de l’Arnon, et jusqu’au mont Siyôn, c’[est] l’Hermon,
fr.B: depuis Aroër, au bord de la vallée de l’Arnon, jusqu’au mont Siyôn, c’est-à-dire l’Hermon,
fr.R: Leur pays allait de la ville d’Aroër, au bord de la vallée de la rivière Arnon, jusqu’au mont Siyôn, au nord, c’est-à-dire le mont Hermon.

sw.L: tangu Aroeri, ulio ukingoni mwa bonde la Arnoni, hadi mlima Siyoni, yaani Hermoni,
sw.B: tangu Aroeri ukingoni mwa bonde la Arnoni hadi Mlima Siyoni, yaani Hermoni,
sw.R: Nchi yao ilienea kutoka mji wa Aroeri, ukingoni mwa bonde la Mto Arnoni, hadi kaskazini kwenye Mlima Siyoni, yaani Mlima Hermoni.

decisions.choice: Siyon: another name for Hermon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew text has "Siyon". This name for Hermon is found only here. The ancient Syriac version has "Sirion", the name 3:9 gives as the Sidonians' name for Hermon, and some think Siyon is a miscopying of it. The text as it stands is followed here.

decisions.choice: from Aroer on the Arnon to Hermon: the whole land east of the Jordan, south to north
decisions.reason: The Arnon gorge was the southern border of Sihon's land (2:36; 3:8, 12), and Mount Hermon the northern limit of Og's (3:8).

decisions.choice: wadi: a valley with a stream that runs in the rainy season
decisions.reason: The word names a valley or gorge and the stream in it. The Arnon cuts a deep gorge into the plateau east of the Dead Sea.

decisions.choice: Their land went ... all the way north
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and adds "north" so readers can follow the boundary.

source.text: וְכָל־הָ֨עֲרָבָ֜ה עֵ֤בֶר הַיַּרְדֵּן֙ מִזְרָ֔חָה וְעַ֖ד יָ֣ם הָעֲרָבָ֑ה תַּ֖חַת אַשְׁדֹּ֥ת הַפִּסְגָּֽה׃פ

records.literal_gloss: and all the Arabah across the Jordan eastward, and to [the] sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of the Pisgah.

en.L: and all the Arabah across the Jordan eastward, and as far as the sea of the Arabah, under the slopes of Pisgah.
en.B: and all the Arabah across the Jordan to the east, as far as the Sea of the Arabah, below the slopes of Pisgah.
en.R: It also included all the Jordan Valley on the east side of the river, as far south as the Dead Sea, below the slopes of Mount Pisgah.

es.L: y todo el Arabá al otro lado del Jordán, al oriente, y hasta el mar del Arabá, bajo las laderas del Pisga.
es.B: y todo el Arabá al otro lado del Jordán, al este, hasta el mar del Arabá, al pie de las laderas del Pisga.
es.R: También incluía todo el valle del Jordán al lado este del río, hasta el mar Muerto en el sur, al pie de las laderas del monte Pisga.

fr.L: et toute l’Araba au-delà du Jourdain, vers l’orient, et jusqu’à la mer de l’Araba, sous les pentes du Pisga.
fr.B: et toute l’Araba au-delà du Jourdain, à l’est, jusqu’à la mer de l’Araba, au bas des pentes du Pisga.
fr.R: Il comprenait aussi toute la vallée du Jourdain, à l’est du fleuve, jusqu’à la mer Morte au sud, au pied des pentes du mont Pisga.

sw.L: na Araba yote ng'ambo ya Yordani upande wa mashariki, hadi bahari ya Araba, chini ya miteremko ya Pisga.
sw.B: na Araba yote ng'ambo ya Yordani upande wa mashariki, hadi Bahari ya Araba, chini ya miteremko ya Pisga.
sw.R: Pia ilijumuisha bonde lote la Yordani upande wa mashariki wa mto, hadi Bahari Mfu upande wa kusini, chini ya miteremko ya Mlima Pisga.

decisions.choice: the Arabah: the deep rift valley of the Jordan and the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: The word means dry or desert land. It names the low valley through which the Jordan runs south into the Dead Sea (1:1; 3:17).

decisions.choice: the sea of the Arabah: the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: It is also called the Salt Sea (3:17; Joshua 3:16).

decisions.choice: slopes: the hillsides running down from Pisgah
decisions.reason: The word is rare and may mean slopes or the springs at their foot. It is the same phrase as in 3:17.

decisions.choice: the Jordan Valley ... the Dead Sea
decisions.reason: Readable uses the names a modern reader knows, as at 3:17.
